trials.name: TOGETHER (AH0003)
trials.population: Prodromal to mild Alzheimer's disease (aged 50-80 years) with cerebral Aβ accumulation and global CDR score 0.5-1.0
trials.primary_endpoint: Change from Baseline to Week 80 in the Clinical Dementia Rating Scale Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) total score
trials.results_summary: The trial failed to meet its primary clinical endpoint (CDR-SB) in the overall population. Bepranemab did slow tau accumulation (a secondary endpoint) by 33-58%. Post-hoc subgroup analyses suggested a slowing of clinical progression (29% on CDR-SB) exclusively in patients with low baseline tau or who were APOE4 non-carriers.

trials.name: PSP003
trials.population: Participants with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP) Richardson's Syndrome
trials.primary_endpoint: Incidence of treatment emergent adverse events (TEAEs) from Baseline to the last Visit (Week 68)
trials.results_summary: Evaluated the safety, tolerability, and biomarker effects of bepranemab in a progressive supranuclear palsy population; results have been peer-reviewed and published.

trials.name: PSP002
trials.population: Rollover participants from the PSP003 trial with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy
trials.primary_endpoint: Incidence of treatment emergent adverse events from Baseline of the open-label extension to the end of the study

trials.name: UP0047
trials.primary_endpoint: The incidence of Adverse Events (AEs) during the study
trials.results_summary: Showed acceptable safety and evaluated the pharmacokinetics of single ascending intravenous doses in healthy males.

trials.name: UP0065
trials.primary_endpoint: The incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events during the study from first dose of UCB0107 to safety follow-up
trials.results_summary: Demonstrated the safety, tolerability, and PK profiles of single doses of bepranemab in a healthy Japanese population.

related_evidence.description: UCB press release detailing the full results of the TOGETHER Phase 2a trial, disclosing the missed primary endpoint and sub-group findings.
Publication in BMJ Neurol Open detailing the Phase 1 healthy volunteer studies (UP0047 and UP0065).
Publication in BMJ Neurol Open detailing the safety, tolerability, and biomarker results in the PSP003 phase 1b trial.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence base for bepranemab is characterized by a major discrepancy between published biomarkers and established clinical efficacy. The analyzed document claims a clinical benefit based exclusively on a secondary endpoint (slowing of tau accumulation via PET imaging). However, UCB's announcements reveal that the TOGETHER Phase II trial (NCT04867616) failed to meet its actual primary endpoint (CDR-SB) in the full intent-to-treat population. While target engagement is clear across early-phase studies in both Alzheimer's disease and Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP), the only signals of clinical disease modification come from post-hoc subgroup analyses (low-tau and APOE4 non-carriers). Until these subgroup hypotheses are confirmed in prospectively powered trials, the claim of broad clinical benefit for bepranemab in prodromal-mild Alzheimer's disease is unsupported by the primary outcome data.
discrepancies: The document claims bepranemab 'demonstrated a clinical benefit', but omits that the TOGETHER Phase II trial (NCT04867616) failed to meet its primary clinical endpoint (CDR-SB) in the overall population.

The document focuses entirely on the tau PET biomarker findings (a secondary endpoint) to substantiate its conclusions, while failing to report the negative primary clinical findings of the same trial.
